about: gst_mrtsdemux_parity_test.py's allowlist (plan ch. 7 WI-P3-4, register B-124): each difference between stock tsdemux 1.28.2 and mrtsdemux that the parity harness lets pass, and why. One entry per rule of the comparison, each used by the run; `measuredEqual` holds the brief's anticipated entries the run shows equal (no entry, so equality is pinned); `excluded` the fixtures left out. Source references are gst-plugins-bad 1.28.2, gst/mpegtsdemux/.

entries.what: Buffer PTS, DTS and duration: their values, and whether each is set.
entries.reason: The point of the element (R-P3-2): mrtsdemux stamps each unit by the formula (PES - 1 h, ceil; B-122), tsdemux by its PCR skew against the input stamps. tsdemux holds a program's first units until its first PCR mapping and leaves their DTS unset where the PES carries none (check_pending_buffers, tsdemux.c:2615, :2735-2747), where mrtsdemux sets DTS = PTS; mrtsdemux gives a 302M unit its duration from the AES3 header (B-121), tsdemux none. gst_mrtsdemux_element_test.py holds mrtsdemux's times to the .demux.jsonl expectations.

entries.what: Where the PMT section message falls among the plan's events: right before the program's collection message in mrtsdemux, right after its no-more-pads in tsdemux.
entries.reason: S14: mrtsdemux posts the PAT and the PMT before the pads so that the muxer's sync-message hooks read the class set before any pad (mux_routing.py _watch_pmts, mux_routing.cpp); tsdemux posts each section after handling it (mpegts_base_handle_psi, mpegtsbase.c:1293-1331), so its PMT follows the program's pads and no-more-pads. The PAT's place is the same in both, and the sequence of section messages is held equal.

entries.what: A second PMT message from mrtsdemux for a PMT whose content changed while its version number stayed; at most one per such change the recording shows.
entries.reason: tsdemux's section filter skips a section whose table, version and section number it has seen, without reading its CRC (seen_section_before, mpegtspacketizer.c:159, :1231), so it never sees the change; DemuxCore posts each changed PMT of its program (B-121). Measured on tp-h264-ac3-eac3-system-b, where ffmpeg fills the AC-3 descriptor in at version 0: the pads stay in both, the (PID, stream type) list being unchanged. The same filter keeps tsdemux's AVC pads on the synthetic syn-mpts-two-programs, whose AVC to HEVC change keeps version 0, where mrtsdemux re-plans (excluded below).

entries.what: A repeated PAT or PMT message from tsdemux (same PID and version) after a continuity loss on that PID; at most one per loss the recording shows on it.
entries.reason: After a CC discontinuity on a section PID tsdemux's packetizer passes the next section by its seen-section filter (the !cc_discont test, mpegtspacketizer.c:1231) and posts the unchanged table again; DemuxCore posts a PAT when it is new and a PMT when the table changed. Measured on cap-cc-loss, whose PMT packet is lost once (the PAT the same way where a source restart resets every counter: syn-source-restart, synthetic). A muxer hook that reads the PMT reads the same table again; nothing re-plans in either.

entries.what: tsdemux's element warning 'CONTINUITY: Mismatch packet ...' at a continuity loss; at most one per loss the recording shows on that PID.
entries.reason: tsdemux posts GST_ELEMENT_WARNING at each CC mismatch while it collects a PES (gst_ts_demux_handle_packet, tsdemux.c:3916-3930); mrtsdemux counts the losses instead (cc-lost and pes-dropped-cc, in its interval message and properties; B-60, B-123), so a lossy input does not post a warning per lost packet to the bus and the engine's log.

entries.what: DISCONT on mrtsdemux's first unit after a continuity loss, where tsdemux sets none; at most one per loss the recording shows on that PID (shared with cc-loss-next-pes).
entries.reason: DemuxCore drops the PES a loss cuts and flags the next unit DISCONT (B-60), so a parser or decoder downstream resyncs; tsdemux drops the cut PES and flags nothing, as it sets DISCONT only on a pad's first buffer after a start, a flush or a DISCONT input buffer (stream->discont, tsdemux.c:2226, :2328).

entries.what: A unit mrtsdemux delivers, flagged DISCONT, that tsdemux drops: the PES whose first packet comes right after a continuity loss; at most one per loss on that PID (shared with cc-loss-discont).
entries.reason: At a CC mismatch tsdemux clears its state and does not process the mismatching packet ('Clear pending state and don't process packet', gst_ts_demux_handle_packet, tsdemux.c:3932-3945), so when that packet starts a PES the whole PES is lost; DemuxCore drops only the PES the loss cut and delivers the next whole PES with DISCONT. Measured on cap-cc-loss's Opus PID (one 328-byte packet).

entries.what: A GAP event on a pad that is not sparse, followed by a DISCONT unit, from mrtsdemux only.
entries.reason: DemuxCore's jump rule (B-121, S5): an audio PES more than two frames after the previous one's end, or a video hole of 1 s or more, is a GAP of the hole and DISCONT on the next unit, so a consumer keeps the house timeline over the hole instead of closing it; tsdemux has no such rule. A bus gap marker's GAPs are marker-gaps. Measured at the gate source's 100 ms steps in cap-mux-align7-aac-opus and cap-cc-loss (two GAPs of about 80 ms on the AAC pad).

entries.what: The number and places of a sparse pad's GAP events, beyond the GAP(0, 0) both push at the pad's start.
entries.reason: mrtsdemux keeps a sparse pad (teletext, DVB subtitles, KLV, ID3) within sparse-gap-lag (500 ms) of program time by GAPs behind it (B-121); tsdemux sends a GAP of duration 0 at the PCR less 800 ms to a pad that pushed nothing since its last check, and checks only when a stream's PTS has run 2 s past its reference (gst_ts_demux_check_and_sync_streams, tsdemux.c:3069; its trigger in gst_ts_demux_push_pending_data, :3861-3880). A cue consumer needs its clock to advance between cues, which both give.

entries.what: tsdemux's last unit on a pad when it is that PID's last PES, bounded and cut short by the end of the stream (its payload as the recording holds it).
entries.reason: At EOS tsdemux pushes what its open PES holds (gst_ts_demux_drain, tsdemux.c:4010); DemuxCore drops a bounded PES shorter than its PES_packet_length (B-121; B-123: the last AAC PES of two PIDs of cap-occ-1080i-h264-aac-ttx, 722 bytes). At a trim's cut end, or a source that stops inside a PES, a decoder gets a truncated frame from tsdemux and none from mrtsdemux.

entries.what: GST_BUFFER_FLAG_TAG_MEMORY on the packets and cells mrtsdemux cuts from one PES (Opus, 0x15 KLV).
entries.reason: mrtsdemux makes each packet a region of the PES buffer without a copy (gst_buffer_copy_region in gstmrtsdemux.cpp program_unit), and GStreamer tags a buffer whose memory was added; tsdemux copies each packet into a new buffer (gst_byte_reader_dup_data and gst_buffer_new_wrapped, parse_opus_access_unit, tsdemux.c:3212-3215). The flag is GstBufferPool's bookkeeping (a pool drops a returned buffer's memory when it is set); these buffers come from no pool and no consumer reads it.

entries.what: mrtsdemux's own element messages, structure mrtsdemux, reason interval, program or unknown-stream.
entries.reason: The demux's counters and its plan for the engine (S3, B-123), forwarded by both runners; tsdemux posts no element message but its section messages. Its warnings not-house-time and no-stream fail the run: the replay runs at the recording's own house time and tsdemux's pads are compared one for one, so either means the harness or the element is wrong.

entries.what: A section message from tsdemux of a table it does not know, on a PMT PID: the second packet of a repeated PMT read as a section of its own; at most one per repeat of a PMT that spans two packets or more.
entries.reason: At a section start (PUSI, pointer 0) tsdemux's packetizer empties the PID's section state (mpegts_packetizer_clear_section, mpegtspacketizer.c:213-221) and skips a section it has seen (seen_section_before, :1231-1241), so the PMT's next packet finds nothing open: the accumulate path counts the empty section complete (:1084-1110) and section_start reads the packet's first payload byte as a table id (:1116-1170). Where that byte is not 0xff and the next has its top bit clear, the bytes pass as a short section and are posted (GST_MPEGTS_SECTION_UNKNOWN). Measured on the OCC ingest recordings (bus-occ-ingest, bus-ingest-relock-gap, bus-pmt-change), whose 299-byte PMT from the sender's ffmpeg spans two packets: the second starts 72 00 0f (the last letter of the language code 'tur', its audio type, the next stream's type), read as table 0x72 of 18 bytes, once per repeated PMT. mrtsdemux posts only the PAT and the PMT.

entries.what: A unit tsdemux delivers that mrtsdemux drops: its PES's first packet repeats the PID's last continuity counter with other bytes; at most one per such packet the recording shows, the DISCONT tsdemux puts on it then on mrtsdemux's next unit.
entries.reason: mrts::CcTracker reads a payload packet that carries its PID's last counter as the one duplicate ISO 13818-1 allows (2.4.3.3) and drops it without comparing bytes, so the PES it starts is lost (demux_core.py CcTracker, B-121). tsdemux has no duplicate test: it checks only last + 1, and only while a PES is open (gst_ts_demux_handle_packet, tsdemux.c:3916-3947), and a new program's streams start with the counter unset (gst_ts_demux_stream_added, tsdemux.c:2221-2238). Measured on bus-pmt-change fed in chunks: the restarted sender's first packet on 12 of its 21 AAC PIDs carries counter 8, the last the old sender sent there, and starts a PES, which tsdemux delivers on the new program's pad. Fed as recorded, a bus DISCONT comes first and mrtsdemux still drops it (CcTracker keeps its counters across a bus DISCONT), while tsdemux loses it at a flush (discont-pending): a finding for DemuxCore (B-132).

entries.what: GAP events on a pad that is not sparse, from mrtsdemux only, each made at a bus gap marker (OQ-12) that carries the pad's PID, the pad's next unit DISCONT.
entries.reason: A gap marker buffer (GAP|DISCONT, B-19) gives each PID it carries a GAP [max(horizon, end - length), end) on its pad and DISCONT on the pad's next unit (B-60, S4). The restamp sends one for every PID each 250 ms while its source is away, then one per PID at the relock (its gap/epoch events), so a pad gets a run of GAPs before its next unit. tsdemux reads a marker's adaptation-only packets as nothing and has no GAP for them. Measured on bus-ingest-relock-gap (17 outage markers on all 23 PIDs, then 22 relock markers of one PID each) and bus-pmt-change (11 and 23), fed as recorded; a sparse pad's are sparse-gaps.

entries.what: A unit tsdemux pushes while it takes in a buffer flagged DISCONT, which mrtsdemux drops: the PES open on that pad at that point, whole or cut; at most one per pad per such buffer.
entries.reason: At a DISCONT input tsdemux drains before it flushes: each pad's open PES is pushed as it stands (mpegts_base_chain, mpegtsbase.c:1539-1557; gst_ts_demux_drain, tsdemux.c:4010-4029), cut where its rest was lost. DemuxCore drops every open PES at a bus DISCONT, as bytes may be missing before it (B-121), so no cut frame reaches a decoder. Measured on bus-occ-ingest and bus-ingest-relock-gap, where the srt-input's leaky queue dropped bus buffers and flagged the next DISCONT (DEV4a): a video PES open at each, fed as recorded.

entries.what: A unit mrtsdemux delivers that tsdemux drops: tsdemux held it, waiting for a PCR after a flush, and a buffer flagged DISCONT came before its next unit on that pad.
entries.reason: tsdemux's flush at a DISCONT input (gst_ts_demux_stream_flush, tsdemux.c:2314-2357) sets pending_ts on every stream and, in push mode on a TIME segment, drops the packetizer's PCR observations (mpegtsbase.c:1551), so it holds each new unit until a PCR maps it (gst_ts_demux_push_pending_data, tsdemux.c:3727-3753; check_pending_buffers, :2615); the next flush drops what it holds. The restamp's relock markers come one PID at a time, about three buffers apart, each a flush in tsdemux, so it loses the units that complete between them; mrtsdemux times units by the formula and delivers them. Measured on bus-ingest-relock-gap and bus-pmt-change fed as recorded.

entries.what: DISCONT on tsdemux's unit where mrtsdemux sets none, with a buffer flagged DISCONT taken in since tsdemux's previous unit on that pad.
entries.reason: tsdemux's flush at a DISCONT input flags every stream's next buffer DISCONT (stream->discont, gst_ts_demux_stream_flush, tsdemux.c:2328), whatever PID the buffer concerned. mrtsdemux flags every pad after a bus DISCONT, but a gap marker flags only the pads of the PIDs it carries (their GAP, then DISCONT), and where tsdemux dropped a unit mrtsdemux delivered (discont-pending) mrtsdemux's DISCONT is on that unit. Measured on bus-ingest-relock-gap and bus-pmt-change fed as recorded.

entries.what: A repeated PAT or PMT message from tsdemux (same PID and version) with a buffer flagged DISCONT taken in since its last message on that PID.
entries.reason: At a DISCONT input in push mode tsdemux clears its packetizer's record of the sections it has seen (mpegts_packetizer_clear, mpegtsbase.c:1555), so it posts the next PAT and PMT again; DemuxCore posts a PAT when it is new and a PMT when the table changed, which a bus DISCONT does not do. Measured on bus-occ-ingest, bus-ingest-relock-gap and bus-pmt-change fed as recorded. Nothing re-plans in either.

measuredEqual.why: Equal on every replay: tsdemux pushes upstream's TIME segment as its own (calculate_and_push_newsegment, tsdemux.c:2988-2990: out_segment = segment), which a bus, like the appsrc here, starts at 0; mrtsdemux pushes {TIME, 0, 0, 0} (B-123). Held equal: an upstream segment from elsewhere than 0 would need an entry.

measuredEqual.item: tsdemux's SDT, EIT and TDT section messages
measuredEqual.why: None: tsdemux 1.28.2 reads sections only on the PAT, the PMTs, the private-section streams a PMT lists and PIDs 2, 3, 0x14, 0x15 and 0x1ffb (mpegts_base_reset, mpegtsbase.c:230-251; mpegts_base_activate_program, :1024-1029), so the SDT on 0x11 that 15 of the recordings carry (and the CAT of cap-occ-1080i-h264-21aac-ttx) is never posted, and no recording has a TDT or TOT on 0x14. A recording that brings one fails until an entry says why.

measuredEqual.item: Buffers tsdemux drops before its first PCR
measuredEqual.why: None on a stamped replay: tsdemux holds a program's units until its first PCR mapping, then pushes them all (check_pending_buffers, tsdemux.c:2615), and ignores the PCR after 500 ms of units without one. Fed without input stamps (push mode, a TIME segment), which no bus does, it gives no unit a PTS and drops at EOS the units it still holds: the AAC pads of cap-occ-1080i-h264-21aac-ttx that start late (measured).

None: tsdemux 1.28.2 sets DISCONT only on a pad's first buffer after a start, a flush or a DISCONT input buffer (stream->discont, tsdemux.c:2226, :2328; mpegts_base_chain's drain and flush), never from its timestamps. Each DISCONT mrtsdemux sets beyond those is an entry's: cc-loss-discont, cc-loss-next-pes, jump-gap, marker-gaps, cc-repeat (the DISCONT it moves).

measuredEqual.item: A buffer list's pieces pushed one by one before tsdemux's first PCR mapping
measuredEqual.why: Equal on a stamped replay: every Opus list has the same pieces, index and length in both (no recording carries 0x15 KLV cells). The 212 pushes against 200 that p3-2 measured on tp-opus-51 (B-123) came from an unstamped feed, on which tsdemux holds more of its first units back and pushes their pieces one at a time.

measuredEqual.item: Pads tsdemux makes for stream types outside part 4.2
measuredEqual.why: None: on every recording tsdemux's pads are mrtsdemux's, in order, names, templates and caps; tp-h264-dts's 0x82 has a pad in neither (mrtsdemux reports it once as unknown-stream, B-121).

measuredEqual.item: The re-plan order (part 9: drain the old pads, add the new, remove the old)
measuredEqual.why: bus-pmt-change re-plans (p3-3b, B-132: its sender switched from H.264 to HEVC, a stream-type change on the same PID through the restamp, generation 0 to 1): the plan's events are equal in order at every feed, the old pads' units drained, the new pads added, then the old removed, as p3-2 matched and gst_mrtsdemux_element_test.py cases 4 and 9 hold (B-123). The one difference B-123 names there, tsdemux posting the new collection message before it drains the old pads and mrtsdemux after, is a message's place against buffers, which this comparison does not order (it orders messages against pad events).

excluded.why: Generated, not recorded: their shapes are DemuxCore's cases, held to their .demux.jsonl by gst_mrtsdemux_element_test.py. Stock tsdemux emits nothing in push mode on syn-mpts-two-programs (its video PES carry no PTS) and skips its same-version AVC to HEVC PMT where mrtsdemux re-plans (pmt-same-version's filter).
